title: The Upside of Boundless Energy
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership argues that a leader's visible energy is a hidden advantage because it is both contagious and symbolic. The post says energy spreads from the leader through the team and builds on itself. It adds that people infer commitment from energy, so high energy signals that the work matters. The piece then widens the point for leaders who are not naturally energetic: anyone can deliberately raise their passion around a project they want to signal as important. A Lou Reed quotation reframes energy as a matter of heart rather than speed.
points: Leader energy is contagious, so team members expend more effort when the leader visibly does.
Teams read high energy as a signal of commitment, dedication and focus.
Energy is a choice leaders can make: raising personal energy around a project conveys its importance.
Passion and commitment naturally produce energy, but even less energetic leaders can lead with more enthusiasm.
quotes: Energy from a leader can be highly infectious. When leaders exude high energy, it inspires others to up their game and bring more zest to what they do.
Emanating from the leader, high energy spreads down and throughout the team. It builds on itself as each team member reflects the energy they feel from others.

Team members who observe a leader with a high motor and a boundless energy make a commonsense inference. They view those leaders as more committed, dedicated, and focused than those leaders with lower energy.
In essence, the high energy exhibited by a leader tells the team that the workplace and the work really matter to them.
Any time a leader wants to convey importance to a project or assignment, they can choose to raise their own personal energy around the work.
High-energy leaders may not have more heart and passion for what they do, but everyone thinks they do.
